IS : 9208 - 1979 

Indian Standard 

GUIDE FOR 
PALLETIZATION OF MICA FOR EXPORT 

0; FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 31 July 1979, after the draft finalized by the Pallets 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Move- 
ment and Packaging Division Council. 

0.2 In view of the mechanization of handling of cargo at the terminals 
as well as in ship's holds unitization of load has assumed a very 
important place for the purpos of export. At the various points of 
transportation, unitization has been found to be an extremely useful 
operation for economy in handling. Therefore, it has been considered 
essential to draw up guidelines to facilitate in preparation of palletized 
export cargo. 

0.3 The present standard is intended to help the exporters to take 
advantage of the modern trends in unitization. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard lays guidelines for the palletization of mica for export. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the terms and definitions as given 
in IS : 3971-1976* shall apply. 

3. PACKAGES 

3.1 Mica shall be packed in boxes with the following outside dimensions: 

a) For mica blocks, loose splittings and thins 400 x 600 mm 

b) For book-form splittings 200 x 200 mm 



*Glossary of terms on pallets {first revision ). 

3 



IS : 9208 - 1979 

These dimensions conform to 400 X 600 mm module as given in 
IS : 8470-1977* as a part of the intermodal overall system. 

4. PALLETS 

4.1 Single deck pallets conforming to ( Indian Standard specification for 
expendable pallets ( under preparation ) 5 with four-way free entry are 
recommended for the palletization of mica. 

4.2 The following overall plan dimensions of the pallets are considered 
suitable: 

a) 1 200 X 1 000 mm 

b) 1 200 X 1 200 mm 

c) 1 200 x i 800 mm 

4.3 The general arrangement of packages on the pallets shall be as 
given in Fig. 1. 

4.4 Depending upon the size and thickness, the number of packages on 
one pallet shall be such that the mass of the palletized load does not 
exceed 1 tonne. 

5. PRESERVATIVES 

5.1 The pallet base shall be treated with suitable preservatives to prevent 
it from decay or infestation.
